# OTP Input

A numeric one-time-passcode field. Auto-advances on entry, distributes pasted codes across slots, and supports SMS autofill on mobile. Configure the digit count, size, and error state with plain props.

```tsx
<OTPInput
  length={6}
  placeholder="0"
  label="Verification code"
  hint="Enter the 6-digit code we sent to your phone."
/>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add otp-input
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/otp-input/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { OTPInput } from "@/components/ui/otp-input"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <OTPInput
      length={6}
      onComplete={(code) => verify(code)}
    />
  )
}
```

## Length

`length` sets the number of digit slots, defaulting to `6`. Four-digit PINs and longer codes use the same component; paste a full code into any slot and it spreads across the rest.

```tsx
<OTPInput length={4} placeholder="0" />

<OTPInput length={6} placeholder="0" />
```

## Label & hint

Pass `label` to caption the field and `hint` for helper text below it. The label wires up as the group’s `aria-labelledby` (clicking it focuses the first slot) and the hint as its `aria-describedby`. Add `required` for a destructive asterisk.

```tsx
<OTPInput
  length={6}
  required
  label="Verification code"
  hint="Check your authenticator app."
  placeholder="0"
/>
```

## Sizes

Three sizes: `sm` (40 px slots), `md` (48 px, the default), and `lg` (56 px). Each stays at or above the 40 px minimum touch target.

```tsx
<OTPInput size="sm" length={4} label="Small" placeholder="0" />

<OTPInput size="md" length={4} label="Medium" placeholder="0" />

<OTPInput size="lg" length={4} label="Large" placeholder="0" />
```

## Separators

Split the slots into groups with `separator`: `"dash"` draws a short divider line, `"dot"` renders a centered `·`, or pass any node for a custom mark. Groups default to two even halves; override with `groupSize`.

```tsx
<OTPInput length={6} separator="dash" placeholder="0" />

<OTPInput length={6} separator="dot" placeholder="0" />

<OTPInput length={6} separator="dash" groupSize={2} placeholder="0" />
```

## Digit entry

Every digit you type rises into its slot from below, on the same roll `AnimatedNumber` uses: it travels up on `duration-base` with `ease-out` and reaches full opacity early, so the eye tracks motion rather than a fade. Typing over a digit, or deleting it, lifts the old one up and out as the new one comes in. Each slot keeps its own roll, so typing fast never cuts the previous digit short.

A pasted code fans in left to right, one `--number-roll-stagger` step apart, so it reads in the order you would say it. A code that is already there when the field mounts (`defaultValue`, a restored form) holds still. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` digits simply appear. The slots stay real inputs underneath, so the caret, selection, autofill and screen readers work as usual.

```tsx
<OTPInput length={6} separator="dash" placeholder="0" />
```

## Validation & errors

Input is numeric-only by construction: non-digit characters (and non-numeric pasted content) are stripped before they ever reach a slot, so you never validate the format yourself. For a *wrong code*, pass `hasError` to switch every slot to the destructive border and ring and set `aria-invalid`; pair it with a message below the field. Use `onComplete` to run verification the moment the last slot fills, and `onChange` for keystroke-level state. When `hasError` is set, the `hint` turns destructive so it doubles as the error message, and the row of slots shakes once (see below).

```tsx
<OTPInput
  length={6}
  hasError
  defaultValue="123456"
  label="Verification code"
  hint="That code didn't match. Try again."
/>
```

## Wrong-code shake

A rejected code doesn’t just recolor: the row of slots swings through a damped wobble and settles, so the refusal registers before you’ve read a word of the message. Each swing is weaker than the last and the motion runs on `ease-sine`, which leaves and arrives at zero velocity, so the throws join into one continuous arc rather than a buzz. Only the row moves. The label and the hint hold still, which keeps the error text readable the instant it lands, and the digits stay put so you can repair the one you got wrong instead of retyping all six.

It fires on its own every time `hasError` goes from `false` to `true`, including when the field mounts already in an error state (a form that came back rejected). No extra props: clear the error as the user edits and the next failure shakes again. The motion is decorative, so it is skipped entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion`, where the destructive border, `aria-invalid`, and the hint still carry the verdict.

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("")
const [status, setStatus] = useState("idle")

<OTPInput
  length={6}
  placeholder="0"
  label="Verification code"
  value={value}
  hasError={status === "error"}
  onChange={(next) => {
    setValue(next)
    // Editing retracts the verdict, so the next
    // rejection is a fresh false → true flip.
    if (status !== "idle") setStatus("idle")
  }}
  onComplete={(code) =>
    setStatus(code === "424242" ? "verified" : "error")
  }
  hint={
    status === "error"
      ? "That code didn't match. Try again."
      : status === "verified"
        ? "Code verified."
        : "Enter any 6 digits to see the shake."
  }
/>
```

If you keep `hasError` pinned `true` across attempts, there is no flip to key off and the second identical rejection would sit silent. Change `errorKey` instead: any new value re-arms the shake under a standing error. An attempt counter is the usual choice.

```tsx
const [attempts, setAttempts] = useState(0)

<OTPInput
  length={6}
  placeholder="0"
  label="Verification code"
  value={value}
  // Never retracted while the user re-types...
  hasError={attempts > 0}
  // ...so the attempt count re-arms the shake.
  errorKey={attempts}
  onChange={setValue}
  onComplete={(code) => {
    if (code !== "424242") setAttempts((n) => n + 1)
  }}
/>
```

## Disabled

```tsx
<OTPInput length={6} disabled defaultValue="12" />
```

## FAQ

### What is the difference between onChange and onComplete?

`onChange` fires on every keystroke with the current value, so use it for keystroke-level state. `onComplete` fires once the moment the last slot fills, which is the right place to kick off verification.

### Do I need to validate or filter the input myself?

No. The field is numeric-only by construction: non-digit characters and non-numeric pasted content are stripped before they ever reach a slot, so you never validate the format yourself.

### How do I show a wrong-code error?

Pass `hasError` to switch every slot to the destructive border and ring and set `aria-invalid`. When set, the `hint` text also turns destructive, so it doubles as the error message.

### Does anything move when the code is wrong?

Yes. The row of slots shakes once, so the refusal registers before the message is read. Only the row moves: the label and hint hold still, and the digits stay so you can repair the wrong one instead of retyping all six. The shake is decorative and is skipped entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### The same wrong code twice doesn't shake the second time.

The shake fires when `hasError` goes from `false` to `true`, so a `hasError` that stays pinned true across attempts never re-fires. Either clear it as the user edits, or bump `errorKey` (an attempt counter works) on each rejection to re-arm the shake.

### Can I turn off the digit roll?

It follows `prefers-reduced-motion`: with reduced motion on, digits appear without moving. A prefilled code never rolls on mount, only digits that arrive after it. The visible digit is painted over the real input (which keeps the value, caret and selection), so screen readers and autofill are unaffected.

### How do I split the digits into groups?

Use `separator`: "dash" draws a short divider line, "dot" renders a centered middle dot, or pass any node for a custom mark. Groups default to two even halves; override the chunk size with `groupSize`.

### Does paste and SMS autofill work across the slots?

Yes. Pasting a full code into any slot spreads it across the rest, and on mobile the first slot carries `autoComplete="one-time-code"` so the OS can autofill a code from SMS.

### How are the label and hint wired for accessibility?

The `label` becomes the group's `aria-labelledby` (clicking it focuses the first slot) and the `hint` becomes its `aria-describedby`. Add `required` for a destructive asterisk.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli add otp-input` writes `components/ui/otp-input/`. Import from `@/components/ui/otp-input`:

- Components and helpers: `OTPInput`, `otpInputVariants`
- Types: `OTPInputProps`
- Koala components it installs with it: `label`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `motion`, `tv`
